_about: Tool notes for tool management, read through tool_plan.notes(). Shape: family = the kind of tool; type = the jobs to use it for; antitype = the jobs it looks right for but must not be used for, each with the tool to use instead; limits = what goes wrong even on its own jobs. Evidence: benchmark chats on the free plan (640px or 480p); best_settings are from recorded calls, compared within the same case. Tier rule: free-tier models only. Image models' tiers are from docs/openapi.json; video models have no tier list there, so a video model counts as free when the free-tier benchmark used it. Priority: generation tools first, deterministic code tools last; fewest tool calls; designed text in the generation prompt, add_words_to_media only for captions or overlays on existing media.

families.image edit (redraws): A model redraws the user's picture. Nothing is kept exactly.
families.image by code: The user's picture is kept exactly; code cuts, reshapes or writes on it.
families.video edit (re-generates): A model re-generates the user's video. Nothing is kept exactly.
families.video by code: The user's video is kept exactly; code cuts, reshapes, writes on or joins it.
families.faces: A face or head from one picture onto a person in a photo or video.
families.sound: Music or voice, made as a sound file.
families.subtitles: Spoken words written on the video.
families.image make: A new picture from text, made by a model.
families.video make: A new video from text or from a picture, made by a model.
families.talking video: A person in a picture or video speaks given words.

edit_image.does: Redraws the whole picture from the user's picture and a prompt.
type: Change one object or the background: the car's colour, night for sunset, a beach behind a person (3.3 to 4.7).
Remove an object or clutter (3.3 to 4.0).
A style: film look, anime, black and white (4.0 to 4.7).
The same character or product in new scenes (4.0).

antitype.job: A new shape with nothing added (a crop or a pad)
antitype.why: Without aspect_ratio it keeps the input's shape: a wide photo asked to be square came back 640x384 (1.0 to 1.3). For a new shape with the scene extended, edit_image with aspect_ratio is right.

antitype.job: A caption or overlay on top of the user's photo, a meme caption
antitype.why: Letters are misspelt or moved (2.3, 2.3). Words in a designed picture are generated; fixing a misspelt word in a generated picture is edit_image.

antitype.job: Pictures side by side
antitype.why: Both pictures are redrawn and cropped (1.7 to 2.0).

antitype.job: Colour only, nothing else changed
antitype.why: Small details change too. Close enough for black and white (4.7).

limits: Parts that should stay can change slightly, because the whole picture is redrawn.
An exact change to words already in a picture (1.5x bigger, same font, same centre) is approximate: a run grew 1.78x and redrew the cup. Say so to the user.
edit_image.deciding_question: Should the picture be redrawn, or kept exactly and only reshaped, cut or written on?
edit_image.bench: Right tool: 158 runs, average 3.6. Wrong tool: 129 runs, average 2.6.

best_settings.evidence: Same case: qwen-edit beat flux-2-klein in 15 of 19 cases (3.15 vs 2.58); qwen-image-2.1 beat qwen-edit 6 of 9 (3.74 vs 3.21) and flux-2-klein 3 of 4 (3.54 vs 2.25). flux-2-klein also ignores aspect_ratio (4:5 asked: 2.0; 9:16: 1.8), qwen follows it (4:5: 3.6).
best_settings.conflict: The upstream description of edit_image (openapi_policies.py, #179) suggests flux-2-klein for a Free account. plan_tool_call's output must name the model.
best_settings.tier: free (all models named here are free-tier)

edit_image.test: Test run: 5 (headshot by edit_image, flux-2-klein). Direct call: qwen-image-2.1 made a true navy, flux-2-klein a brighter royal blue; both kept the street. Small gap on a colour edit; the bench gap is on shape and words.

edit_video.does: Re-generates the whole video from the user's video and a prompt.
type: Change how the whole video looks, when the user accepts that it is re-made. Not shown in the bench: it was never the right tool in 36 runs.

antitype.job: A new shape (vertical, square)
antitype.why: Output is about 832x448 or 832x512 whatever was asked (1.0).

antitype.job: A shorter clip, the best part, cut the boring parts
antitype.why: It re-renders the footage instead of cutting it (2.0).

antitype.job: Words or a watermark
antitype.why: The mark was missing (1.0).

limits: Output shape is its own (about 832x512), not the input's.
edit_video.deciding_question: Should the video be re-made, or kept and only cut, reshaped or written on?

generate_music.does: Makes a music track from a style prompt. Sound only.
type: A music bed of 15 s or more (4.0).

antitype.job: Music shorter than 15 s
antitype.why: The API's minimum duration is 15 s: a 10 s request came back 15 s (2.3).

antitype.job: Music on the user's video
antitype.use: generate_music or a voice, then add_sound_to_video
antitype.why: It makes a separate file; nothing puts it on the video (2.0).

generate_music.deciding_question: How long, and on its own or under the user's video?
generate_music.test: Test run: the agent asked 15 s and cut to 10 s (antitype confirmed).

add_subtitles_to_video.does: Transcribes the speech in the video and burns it in as subtitles.
type: Subtitles in the language that is spoken (3.0).

antitype.job: Subtitles in another language
antitype.use: none (a GAP): translate_video changes the speech, not only the subtitles
antitype.why: It writes the spoken language: Spanish asked, English delivered (2.0).

antitype.job: Subtitles and a new shape
antitype.why: It has no shape setting.

antitype.job: A clip with no speech
antitype.use: no call: tell the user there is no speech
antitype.why: The job fails instead of saying so.

limits: The first line is sometimes missing.
add_subtitles_to_video.deciding_question: Same language as the speech, or translated? Does the clip have speech?

best_settings.evidence: highlight 2.79 (14 runs), minimalist 2.47, cinematic 2.42. No same-case comparison; weak.

swap_head_in_photo.does: Puts the whole head from one picture (face, hair, head shape) onto the body in another picture. 10 credits.
swap_head_in_photo.preferred: Use head swap for swapping faces in photos.
type: Put the user's face on someone in a photo, keeping their hair and head shape so they are recognisable.

antitype.job: A face or head swap in a video, one person
antitype.use: get_first_frame, swap_head_in_photo on that frame, then replace_character_in_video (wan-animate or, on the free plan, minimax-h3; style.mode animate)
antitype.why: Head swap is photo only; the animated head-swapped frame keeps the video (test).

antitype.job: Several people in one photo, each with their own new head
antitype.why: No person choice: a second head swap on the whole photo changes everyone (test).

antitype.job: One chosen person in a group photo, if head swap picks the wrong one
antitype.why: Its only settings are body_file_path and head_file_path: no face choice (not tested).

limits: Choosing one person among several is not a setting; ask which person first (this worked).
swap_head_in_photo.deciding_question: Which picture gives the head, and which picture (and which person) receives it?
swap_head_in_photo.bench: 0 runs in the persona bench; 2 tests (4 in a test run; one by eye, a direct call).
swap_head_in_photo.test: Test run: 1.5 → 4 (asked which person, then head swap onto the right one). The astronaut case used swap_face_in_photo (4), so head swap on it is still untested. The astronaut case, direct call: the head swap is clearly the woman in the portrait (curly hair, face shape), suit, stars and retro look kept; the agent's face swap from the test run kept the astronaut's head and looked like a blend.

swap_face_in_photo.does: Puts a face from one picture onto faces in another picture. The face only, not hair or head shape.
type: Only when the user refuses a head swap: the face changes, hair and head shape stay.

antitype.job: A face swap on one person
antitype.why: Only the face changes; hair and head shape stay, so the person is less recognisable (2.0 to 2.3).

antitype.job: Several people in one photo, each with their own new face
antitype.why: individual-faces was a blend; 'should be a head swap'.

swap_face_in_photo.deciding_question: One person, or several people each with their own new face?
swap_face_in_photo.bench: 12 runs, average 3.1 (one case 3.7 to 4.0, another 2.0 to 2.3).

best_settings.evidence: all-faces 3.86 (7 runs), individual-faces 2.00 (5 runs, all on the hard case). Not a fair comparison.

swap_face_in_video.does: Puts a face from a picture onto a person in a video.
type: Several people in one clip, each with their own new face (individual-faces).

antitype.job: One person in a video gets the user's face
antitype.use: get_first_frame, swap_head_in_photo on that frame, then replace_character_in_video (wan-animate or, on the free plan, minimax-h3; style.mode animate)
antitype.why: Face swap: 'should be a head swap'. Test: recognisable, sound kept.

antitype.job: Only part of the clip
antitype.why: Asked for the first 5 s, it delivered all 10 s.

antitype.job: A face swap in a photo
antitype.why: The choice for photos.

limits: The new face is a blend; graders did not recognise the portrait (2.7). Warn the user.
Two faces in one clip: both barely change and the sound was lost (1.0 to 1.3).
One person can be several face crops (a turned head): map each crop of that person, or the old face comes back when the head turns.
swap_face_in_video.deciding_question: Which person, and which part of the clip?

remove_image_background.does: Cuts the subject out of a picture onto a transparent background.
type: A product or person with clear edges.

antitype.job: A logo with thin letters
antitype.use: generate_image with the words in the prompt on a plain background, then this tool, and check the letters (words are generated); if they fade, cut out the logo without words, then add_words_to_media
antitype.why: The letters fade or smear (2.7).

antitype.job: A logo on a video
antitype.why: It only makes the PNG; nothing puts it on the video (1.3).

remove_image_background.deciding_question: Is there text in the picture? Where will the cut-out be used?
remove_image_background.bench: Right tool: 9 runs, average 1.6 (most of it one case, a job no tool finishes).

reframe_media.does: Changes the shape of a picture or video by code: crop, pad (bars of one colour), fill (over a blurred copy) or auto. 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1. 0 credits.
type: Keep a picture or video exactly and only change its shape, when the user wants nothing added (bars, blur or a crop).
A video's new shape (no generative tool extends a video).

antitype.job: A picture's new shape where the scene can be extended
antitype.use: edit_image with the new aspect_ratio, extending the scene
antitype.why: Generation first.
Its shapes are 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1.

antitype.job: Two people who take turns, each centred
antitype.use: trim_media per speaker, reframe_media each with its own focus, join_videos
antitype.why: One focus per call.

limits: Not benchmarked.
Crop loses the edges: set `focus` on the subject (the shoe on the left), or use pad or fill to keep everything.
reframe_media.deciding_question: Crop (lose the edges), or keep everything with bars (pad) or a blurred copy (fill)? Where is the subject?
reframe_media.bench: 0 runs in the persona bench; 3 test runs.
reframe_media.test: Test run (happy user, 1 run each): 1 → 4, 1 → 3 (whole shoe kept with matching padding; it stays small and off-centre), 1 → 4 (9:16 crop with her centred).

trim_media.does: Cuts a video or sound file from `start` to `end` seconds by code. Picture and sound kept. 0 credits.
type: Shorten the user's clip, keep the first N seconds, cut a clip into parts.
Music under 15 s: after generate_music.
A frame at a chosen time: trim to it, then get_last_frame.
Only part of a clip for a face swap: trim first.

antitype.job: A picture
antitype.use: none: it cuts video and sound only
antitype.why: Pictures are refused.

limits: Not benchmarked.
It does not choose the part: 'the best 10 seconds' needs a look at the clip first.
trim_media.deciding_question: Which part, from when to when?
trim_media.bench: 0 runs in the persona bench; 2 test runs.
trim_media.test: Test run: 2.5 → 5 (first 5 s kept exactly). Another case, 3: the cut was right, but the agent picked the part blind (half of it a static lead-in); it cannot see the clip.

add_words_to_media.does: Draws exact words on a picture or video by code: title, caption, price, name, watermark. Always spelled right. 0 credits.
type: A caption on top of the user's photo.
A watermark or caption on a video, for the whole clip or from start to end.
Top and bottom text on a meme made from the user's picture.

antitype.job: Words that are part of a designed picture (headline, poster, flyer, logo, thumbnail, carousel slide)
antitype.use: generate_image or edit_image with the words in the prompt
antitype.why: Generation first; drawn words sit on top and look pasted on.

antitype.job: Words that must look printed on an object (a sign, a label)
antitype.why: Drawn words do not follow the object.

limits: Not benchmarked.
Places: top, middle, bottom, corners. Sizes: small, normal, large. No free position or font choice.
add_words_to_media.deciding_question: The exact words, where, and how big? On an object, or over the picture?
add_words_to_media.bench: 0 runs in the persona bench; 3 test runs.
add_words_to_media.test: Test run: 2 → 4, 1 → 4 (watermark), 4 (generate_image without words, then this tool: headline exact).

mix_audio.does: Lays sound files over each other into one sound file: a voice over music, a podcast intro. Sound only. 0 credits.
type: A voice over music, music first then the voice.

antitype.job: Sound on the user's video
antitype.use: generate_music or a voice, then add_sound_to_video
antitype.why: It outputs sound only, no picture.

limits: Not benchmarked.
mix_audio.deciding_question: Which tracks, from when, and how loud?
mix_audio.test: Test run: 2.5 → 4: 15 s generate_music, cut to 10 s with a fade-out. Also used in another case to fit a voice line.

join_videos.does: Joins videos end to end with hard cuts, or sound files into one sound file. 0 credits.
type: Several clips into one film.
Voice lines made one at a time into one sound file.

antitype.job: A single clip
antitype.why: Called on one clip for no reason in 24 runs (average 2.0).

antitype.job: Sound on a video
antitype.why: It refuses a mix of video and sound files.

limits: Every clip is fitted to the first one's size.
join_videos.deciding_question: Which clips, in what order, with sound or silent?
join_videos.bench: Right tool: 1 run. Wrong tool: 24 runs, average 2.0.

get_last_frame.does: Takes the last frame of a video as a picture. 0 credits.
type: Continue a clip: the last frame becomes the start of create_video_from_image.
A frame at a chosen time: trim_media to it first.

antitype.job: Seeing what is in the video
antitype.use: none: one frame shows only the end
antitype.why: Used to 'look' at clips in 12 runs (average 1.9).

get_last_frame.deciding_question: Is the end of the clip what is needed?
get_last_frame.bench: Right tool: 3 runs. Wrong tool: 12 runs, average 1.9.

detect_faces.does: Finds the faces in a picture or video, for a swap that maps each face.
type: Before swap_face_in_video in individual-faces mode, when several people each get their own face. A photo needs no detect_faces call: swap_heads_in_photo finds the faces itself.

antitype.job: Several people in one photo, each with a new face or head
antitype.why: Test: detect_faces then swap_face_in_photo gave a blend; the faces barely changed.

antitype.job: Any job that is not a per-face swap
antitype.why: Called as an extra step in 30 runs (average 1.9); its face crops were delivered as results.

detect_faces.deciding_question: Do several people each get a different face?
detect_faces.bench: Right tool: 5 runs, average 2.0. Wrong tool: 30 runs, average 1.9.

generate_image.does: Makes pictures from text. Shapes 1:1, 16:9, 9:16. Many models.
type: Product shots, illustrations, scenes (3.3 to 4.5).
Designed pictures with words: headline, poster, flyer, logo, thumbnail, carousel slide; the exact words quoted in the prompt.
limits: Shapes: only 1:1, 16:9, 9:16 in the aspect setting; 4:5 needs another step.
Exact counts and colours drift: about 25 balloons for 3, clear glass for amber.
A vague user's details get lost: a silver bottle on white for 'matte black on marble'; ask, do not guess.
Words can be misspelt (flux-2-klein in the bench). Use qwen-image-2.1, quote the words, check the result; fix with edit_image if wrong.
generate_image.deciding_question: Are there exact words? Exact counts or colours that must be right? What shape?

use.style.tool: ai-illustration-generator for an illustration, else none

best_settings.evidence: Same case: qwen-image-2.1 beat flux-2-klein in 11 of 14 cases (3.24 vs 2.43) and z-image-turbo 6 of 8 (3.37 vs 2.45). style.tool ai-illustration-generator beat none 8 of 8 (3.57 vs 2.74); ai-photo-generator lost to none 5 of 5 (2.60 vs 3.20); movie-poster-generator lost 2 of 2.
best_settings.tier: free (all models named here are free-tier)

create_video_from_text.does: Makes a video from text. 1 to 60 s; 16:9, 9:16, 1:1.
type: A short clip of a scene (3.2).

antitype.job: Changing the user's video
antitype.why: It makes a new video, nothing of the user's is kept.

antitype.job: A label or exact words in the video
antitype.why: Labels missing.

limits: Motion of objects can be wrong: the frisbee passes through the dog.
Most of its runs are video composition items; for single clips the bench has few cases.
create_video_from_text.deciding_question: How long, what shape, with sound or silent?

best_settings.evidence: Sound test, 60 clips: minimax-h3 made the scene sound in every case; ltx-2.5 missed wind, the background under a voice, a second speaker and the second line of a two-line clip. minimax-h3 for single clips too; ltx-2.5 only for a clip over 30 s (minimax-h3 makes at most 30 s). Older bench: ltx-2.5 beat default in 11 of 16 cases (2.24 vs 1.97).
best_settings.tier: free (all models named here are free-tier)

create_video_from_image.does: Animates a picture into a video. 1 to 60 s. Keeps the picture's shape.
type: Bring a picture to life (4.0, reels 3.0 to 3.3).
Continue a clip from its last frame.

antitype.job: A still end card
antitype.use: make_card_clip with attach after: the clip and the card come back as one file, no join_videos
antitype.why: It adds motion and the card came out 2 s instead of 9.

limits: The motion asked for may not happen: a push-in zoom for a quarter turn of the bottle.
No shape setting: reframe_media after if a shape was asked.
create_video_from_image.deciding_question: What should move, and how long?

upscale_image.does: Enlarges a picture. Modes: pro, preserve, balanced, creative.
type: Make a sharp picture bigger (4.8).

antitype.job: Restore an old photo, keep the faces
antitype.use: test edit_image first; use mode preserve
antitype.why: Faces were regenerated with broader smiles and different features (2.0).

limits: Scale is a factor (2x): a 640 px long edge is not hit exactly (480x480).
A very blurry photo is only slightly cleaner (2.0).
upscale_image.deciding_question: Bigger only, or also fixed? How big?

best_settings.evidence: Undecided. Persona bench: preserve 3.10 (20 runs) vs balanced 2.0 (2 runs), no same-case pair. Same case, one run each: balanced 3, preserve 2 (faces redrawn with broader smiles). Test both before choosing.

upscale_image.test: Test run: 2 → 3 with mode preserve: clean 640 sepia enlargement, faces smoothed and slightly altered (limit confirmed). Dry run with preserve: 2 (faces redrawn); another case with the planner: 4.

generate_headshot.does: Makes a professional headshot from a photo of a person.
type: A professional headshot (4.0).

antitype.job: A square headshot or a set background
antitype.why: It returned 928x1152 portrait, framed to the waist, and an office background for 'plain grey' (3.0).

limits: No shape or background setting.
generate_headshot.deciding_question: Shape and background, or the tool's own?

create_meme.does: Makes a meme from a topic on a known template.
type: A meme about a topic, the template chosen by the tool (3.5).

antitype.job: A meme with the user's own picture and exact words
antitype.why: It uses its templates and writes its own caption.

limits: Captions can break mid-word or overflow the panel, and drift off the topic (a weekend joke for 'Mondays').
create_meme.deciding_question: The user's picture and words, or a template and a joke on a topic?

create_talking_photo.does: Makes a photo of a person speak given words.
type: A photo of the user saying a line (4.0).

antitype.job: A set shape
antitype.why: It keeps the photo's shape: 1024x1536 for 'square'.

limits: Resolution 480p or 720p.

The clip is as long as asked even when the speech is shorter: an 8 s clip with 4.5 s of speech ends with 3 s of silence, or repeats the line's start ("Hi ev" again at 4.9 s). Longer than the line: pad the line with silence first (mix_audio `seconds`).
Lip movement failed in 1 of 2 test runs.
create_talking_photo.deciding_question: The exact line, and the shape?
create_talking_photo.test: Test runs: 2 (mouth closed in the sampled frames); 4 (mouth moves with the speech, square, no captions). One bad run in two.

create_spoken_ad_video.does: Makes a short ad video of a person speaking (UGC ad). Models kling-3.0, ltx-2.5, veo3.1.
type: A talking ad from a picture and a line (4.0, 4.0).
limits: Length: 5 s came back for 8 s asked; check the length setting.

create_lip_sync_video.does: Makes a person in a video mouth a given audio track.
type: The person on screen says new words (an on-screen presenter).

antitype.job: A voice-over with no presenter, or the original footage kept as it is
antitype.use: generate_music or a voice, then add_sound_to_video
antitype.why: It re-made the footage at 832x448, details changed; black clips and burned-in captions (1.7).

limits: Few runs (5).
create_lip_sync_video.deciding_question: Is a person on screen who should speak the words?

add_sound_to_video.does: Lays music and/or a voice-over on the user's video by code: the picture is kept, nothing is generated, 0 credits. Built for tool management, on the shared media_tools.add_sound.
type: Music under the user's clip.
A voice-over on the user's clip, or a narration in place of its sound.
Music under speech in the clip, the speech kept clear (radio calls): original=keep.

antitype.job: Sound on its own, no video
antitype.why: This tool needs a video.

antitype.job: Making the music or the voice
antitype.use: generate_music, or the voice generator, first
antitype.why: It only mixes sound that exists.

limits: Not benchmarked yet; tested on generated test clips (tests/test_tool_media.py).
A voice longer than the video is read up to a little faster, then the last frame is held: the video gets longer.
original=keep keeps everything heard in the clip clear, not only speech (it finds sound by loudness).
add_sound_to_video.deciding_question: Keep the video's own sound clear, lower it, or replace it?

adjust_colours.does: Changes only the colours of a picture or video by code: warmth, saturation (0 = black and white), brightness, contrast. Nothing redrawn, 0 credits. Built for tool management.
type: Warmer or cooler.
Black and white.
Brighter or more contrast.

antitype.job: Change the colour of one object (the car navy)
antitype.why: It changes the whole picture's colours, not one object.

limits: Not benchmarked yet; tested on generated pictures and clips.
Warmth 0.3 is a clear but gentle change; 0.6 is strong.
adjust_colours.deciding_question: Which colour change, and how strong?

put_pictures_side_by_side.does: Puts 2 to 4 pictures into one (row, column, 2x2 grid), each whole: scaled to fit, never cropped, stretched or redrawn; optional exact labels. 0 credits.
type: Before and after.
A comparison or a collage of the user's photos.

antitype.job: A made-up after picture
antitype.use: edit_image first for the new picture, then this tool with the original and the new one
antitype.why: This tool only arranges pictures that exist.

limits: Not benchmarked yet.
Pictures of different shapes leave padding (background colour) around them.
put_pictures_side_by_side.deciding_question: Which pictures, in what order, what layout and shape, labels?

put_picture_on_video.does: Puts a picture (a logo; transparent PNG kept) on a video or picture, in a corner or the centre, sized, see-through, for all or part of a clip. Video kept exactly, 0 credits.
type: A logo on the user's video for the whole clip.

antitype.job: Text or a handle as a watermark
antitype.why: Words are drawn exactly by add_words_to_media.

limits: Not benchmarked yet.
A logo with a white background shows the white box: remove_image_background first.
put_picture_on_video.deciding_question: Where, how big, for how long?

make_card_clip.does: Makes a still card as a clip, with a silent sound track and the size of a given clip, so join_videos can add it. 0 credits. The card itself is generated first (generate_image or edit_image) and given as `picture`, background none.
type: An end card or title card attached to the user's clip in one call (attach=after or before).

antitype.job: A moving title or animation
antitype.why: The card is still.

antitype.job: Drawing the card's words on a flat colour by code
antitype.use: generate_image (qwen-image-2.1, words quoted), then this tool with the picture
antitype.why: Every card is generated; a drawn card only when the user asks for one. A small misspelling on a generated card is kept (the code words looked worse).

limits: Not benchmarked yet.
Words: one line each, the first larger; no font choice.
make_card_clip.deciding_question: Which words, which colour, how long, before or after?

change_clothes_in_photo.does: Puts the clothes from an outfit picture on a person in a photo.
type: A person photo and an outfit picture; garment_type picks the top, the bottom or the whole outfit.

antitype.job: An outfit given only in words
antitype.why: This tool needs an outfit picture.

limits: Costs 25 credits.
Needs both pictures.
change_clothes_in_photo.deciding_question: Is the outfit a picture or words?
change_clothes_in_photo.bench: Draft from the tool's inputs; no bench runs yet.

place_person_in_scene.does: Puts the person from one photo into a scene picture.
type: A person photo and a scene picture.

antitype.job: A scene given only in words
antitype.use: generate_image the scene first, then this tool
antitype.why: This tool needs a scene picture.
